p3_b5.ocr: 1Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas 2Accessibility/Remoteness Index of Australia are similar to those for algorithms developed using UK [11] and US data [14]. The false positive rate (37.5%) for this study (at a risk-score threshold of 50%) was similar to, although slightly higher than, that reported in the UK (34.7%) and US (34.1%). The sensitivity for this study was 44.7% (at a risk-score threshold of 50%), which is similar to, although slightly lower than, the correspond- ing percentages obtained from the UK (54.3%) and US (57.9%) studies. The ROC score for this study was modest (0.65), and similar to that for the UK (0.69) study. (We could not locate a published ROC score for the US study.)

p3_b6.ocr: Likelihood ratios are a convenient way of summarising the performance of a predictive algorithm (Table 3). LR+ for the Australian and UK and US algorithms were gener- ally fair, but all the LR- were poor and for higher risk-score thresholds they were close to 1.0. This is because algo- rithms based on routine inpatient data have poor sensitiv- ity (i.e., large percentage of false negatives). To give this some context, LR- associated with carcinoembryonic anti- gen (CEA) for detecting early colorectal cancer are also close to 1.0, so that after some initial enthusiasm [22], it was decided that CEA should not used as screening test for colorectal cancer.
